value.placement_reason: The 2 x callout identifies the two M5 holes. The printed 82,0 dimension locates the left hole from the central vertical axis; the opposed two-hole layout establishes its mirrored partner at X=+82. Both lie on the horizontal hole axis dimensioned 4,5 above Y=0.

The 17,9 dimension directly locates the first lower-row hole right of the central vertical axis. The 7,5 dimension locates the lower hole axis below Y=0. The 8 x M3 callout establishes this hole's printed drill diameter, thread and through operation without requiring the other six unresolved placements.

The printed 35,7 dimension connects the first lower-row hole right of center, located by 17,9, to the next hole to its right. Thus this hole is at X=17.9+35.7=53.6 on the axis dimensioned 7,5 below Y=0. This uses only the displayed dimension chain, without extending that spacing to undimensioned holes.

The 4 x slot callout, horizontal layout, printed 82,0 adjacent-slot spacing and 41,0 centerline-to-inner-right-slot offset establish slot centers at X=-123,-41,41,123. Their long axes follow the drawing's vertical axis. The 2,3 vertical dimension locates the lower semicircle center above Y=0, so each overall slot center is at Y=2.3+(10.0-5.5)/2=4.55; the separate 4,5 M5-hole dimension is not substituted for this slot location.

sources.note: The original main view supports the two M5 - 6H through holes, four vertical 5,5 X 10,0 through slots, and two individually located M3 - 6H through holes at X=17.9 and X=17.9+35.7. The remaining six M3 horizontal positions are unresolved. Printed drill diameters and through-thread callouts establish the retained holes independently of the omitted placements. Verification: In D-013's main view, the vertical centreline is X=0 and the horizontal centreline is Y=0 (it splits the 25,0 height). M5 pair: callout p1-1 gives 2 x Ø4,2 THRU ALL M5 - 6H. The left 82,0 (n/82.0@1-1, box ~x489pt) runs from the left M5 hole to the centreline, and the right M5 hole sits in the opposed mirrored position. 4,5 (n/4.5@1-1) locates both on the axis above Y=0. So x=0-n0=-82 and a 2-count row with spacing n0*2=164 along 0° is correct. M3 holes: n/17.9@1-1 runs from the centreline extension to the first hole right of centre. n/35.7@1-1 runs from that hole to the next one, so x=17.9 and x=n0+n1=53.6 are directly dimensioned. 7,5 (n/7.5@1-1) runs from Y=0 to the lower hole axis, so y=-7.5. The Ø2,5 THRU ALL M3 - 6H values come from p1-2. Slots: callout p1-3 gives 4 x 5,5 X 10,0 THRU ALL. 41,0 (n/41.0@1-1) runs from the centreline to the inner right slot, and the right 82,0 (n/82.0@1-2) runs from there to the outer right slot. The left slots mirror these, so a uniform 82 pitch from -123 gives -123,-41,41,123; this matches 41+41=82 across the centre. The slot long axes are drawn vertical. 2,3 (n/2.3@1-1) runs from Y=0 to the lower arc centre of the right slot, which is marked with crosshairs. That gives a slot centre of n0+(n1-n2)/2=4.55, and the slot bottom at -0.45 sits just below the centreline, matching the view. Numeric values, cited IDs, expressions and ordering (holes by x ascending, then slots) are all consistent.

sources.note: The original drawing supports the rectangular constant-thickness base-body contract with the permitted minor omissions stated explicitly. Verification: Drawing D-013 shows the part from the front, from the side and in isometric. All three show one flat plate. Its outer outline is rectangular, and it has no bends, steps, revolved shape or grooves. The side view is a single rectangle of uniform width. The isometric view also shows uniform thickness along the full length. The stacked '6,0 / 3,0' thickness label sits on one dimension line. That is a printed choice between thickness values, which the contract allows. It is not a step in the body, so the exact value can be settled in the detailed fields. The front view has small straight corner clips at all four corners. They have no dimensions, and the side view shows matching lines near its ends. These fit the allowance for small undimensioned corner clips on an established rectangle. They are not a custom rounded or angled outer contour. The title-block note 'DEBURR AND BREAK SHARP EDGES' (D-013/drawing/general/edge_finish) supports omitting edge breaks. The slots and holes are internal through-cuts and do not change the base-body contract. supported=true, constant_thickness=true, outline_exact=true and an empty essential_uncertainty are all consistent with this evidence.
